name: agents-inc-monorepo
//: Prettier is declared once, here. Prettier walks up from each file to the nearest config, so this covers every workspace including packages/*-config. It is also why packages/cli keeps its own formatting for free: packages/cli/prettier.config.mjs sits nearer to the CLI's files than this field does, so it wins for everything under packages/cli and this config never touches them. Prettier does NOT walk up for .prettierignore, which is why `format` runs from the root rather than fanning out through turbo — see the scripts below.

scripts.//prepare: Moved here from packages/cli when the CLI stopped being the repository root. Git hooks live in .husky/ at the root of the repository, so the package that installs them has to be the root package.
scripts.//format: One run from the root, deliberately not `turbo format`. Prettier reads .prettierignore only from its working directory, so fanning out per workspace made the root ignore invisible and reformatted the vendored catalog it exists to protect — which then reads as drift against the generator. The glob stays as it was: widening it to md/json is a separate decision, not part of fixing this.

//lint-staged: Formatting only. ESLint used to sit here as a second entry, carried over from when packages/cli was the repository root and its eslint.config.js therefore sat beside .husky/. lint-staged runs its commands from the git root, and ESLint 9 flat config is looked up from the working directory and its ancestors — never beside the file being linted — so after the merge that entry failed on every commit staging a .ts file. It cannot be repaired in place: each workspace keeps its own eslint.config.js one level down, and packages/cli is on ESLint 9 while apps/* and the other packages/* are on ESLint 10, so no single config and no single binary at the root could lint them all. Linting moved to the turbo line in .husky/pre-commit, which gives each workspace its own eslint in its own directory. Prettier stays here precisely because it does NOT want per-workspace working directories — see the note on `format` above.
